Find and extract the item lists from the July 2, 1959 edition of “United States Standards for Grades of Processed Fruits, Vegetables, and Certain Other Products.” Objective: produce a complete, audit-ready list of entries specifically in (a) the Dried and Dehydrated section and (b) the Frozen/Chilled section, preserving the exact item names and whether each line is labeled Dehydrated, Frozen, or Chilled.

Scope and constraints:
- Primary goal: obtain the authoritative 1959 edition with cover/date July 2, 1959. Acceptable sources include USDA AMS official PDFs, Government Publishing Office, National Archives, HathiTrust, Google Books, Internet Archive, or university library scans; prioritize government/AMS sources if available.
- Ensure the copy contains the complete list sections and is not an excerpt; confirm headings “Dried and Dehydrated” and “Frozen/Chilled.”
- If multiple scans exist, select the one clearly dated July 2, 1959 and containing both sections. If only near-dated editions are available (e.g., 1958 or 1960), gather them to cross-validate, but clearly mark any deviation from July 2, 1959.

Extraction requirements:
- For each entry in the Dried and Dehydrated section: capture the exact line as printed (verbatim item title), and note whether it is specifically marked as “dehydrated.” Only list entries that actually appear under this section, but include all entries (some may be dried but not dehydrated; mark them accordingly because we will filter later).
- For each entry in the Frozen/Chilled section: capture the exact line as printed, and mark whether it’s “Frozen” or “Chilled.”
- Preserve exact spelling, capitalization, punctuation, hyphenation, and plural/singular. Include any parenthetical qualifiers that are part of the item name.
- Provide page numbers (or image numbers) and a working URL for each source. If the item lists span multiple pages, indicate the page range.

Deliverables:
1) A structured table for the Dried and Dehydrated section with columns: Section, Item Name (exact string), Marker (e.g., Dehydrated, Dried—if printed as such), Page(s), Source URL.
2) A structured table for the Frozen/Chilled section with columns: Section, Item Name (exact string), Marker (Frozen or Chilled), Page(s), Source URL.
3) Short narrative on source verification (why this is the July 2, 1959 edition, any confirmatory evidence such as title page date or AMS identifier), and any gaps or ambiguities (e.g., missing pages, illegible lines).
4) If the July 2, 1959 edition cannot be found with both sections intact, list the best alternative sources used, detail differences, and include images/text excerpts for the relevant lists.

Notes for later steps (context for extraction fidelity):
- We will later match Frozen entries to dehydrated items by "contains the whole name" logic, so precise item strings are critical; do not normalize or reinterpret.
- If the scan includes a consolidated index or cross-reference that enumerates the same items, capture that too (with citation), but keep the primary list as the canonical source.

Determine supersession status (post–July 2, 1959 and pre–August 2023) for the following 1959 USDA/AMS grade standards, using authoritative sources (USDA AMS official standards PDFs/pages, Federal Register, GPO/National Archives CFR). Classify each as Superseded (Yes: newer version issued/revised), Not superseded (withdrawn or no replacement), or Uncertain. Provide citations (URLs), document titles, effective/revision dates, and any “Supersedes” notes. If names changed or standards were consolidated, document the mapping and justify counting as superseded.

Source 1959 compilation (for context): https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/06/United_States_standards_for_grades_of_processed_fruits%2C_vegetables%2C_and_certain_other_products_%28as_of_July_2%2C_1959%29_%28IA_unitedstatesstan14unit_4%29.pdf (pages 5–6).

Denominator items (Primary interpretation A: commodity-name containment):
1) Apples, Dehydrated (Low-moisture) 2/ [Commodity name: Apples]
2) Grapefruit Juice (Dehydrated) 2/ [Commodity name: Grapefruit Juice]
3) Orange Juice (Dehydrated) 2/ [Commodity name: Orange Juice]
4) Apples (Frozen)
5) Grapefruit Juice, Concentrated (Frozen)
6) Grapefruit Juice and Orange Juice, Concentrated, Blended (Frozen)
7) Orange Juice, Concentrated (Frozen)

Alternative interpretation B (exact-string containment) has only items 1–3; please still research item-level supersession for completeness.

Research instructions:
- For each item, locate the most relevant AMS grade standard(s) for the same commodity/style (e.g., “United States Standards for Grades of Dehydrated Apples (Low-moisture)”, “United States Standards for Grades of Frozen Apples”, “United States Standards for Grades of Frozen Concentrated Grapefruit Juice”, “United States Standards for Grades of Frozen Concentrated Orange Juice”, and any standard covering “Blended Grapefruit and Orange Juice, Frozen Concentrate”).
- Determine whether a newer version exists after July 2, 1959 (reissued/revised, with dates). Show evidence such as “Effective [date]”, “Revised [date]”, or “Supersedes [older date]”. If a standard was withdrawn with no replacement, mark Not superseded (withdrawn) and provide a withdrawal notice link.
- If a single modern document covers multiple commodities (e.g., combined citrus frozen concentrates), ensure mapping is clear. If the modern title changed slightly but clearly covers the same commodity/style (e.g., “Frozen Concentrated Orange Juice” vs. “Orange Juice, Concentrated (Frozen)”), count as superseded and justify briefly.
- For ambiguous items like “Apples (Frozen)”, verify the existence of a specific frozen apples standard; if none exists, check if it was withdrawn historically or never had a standalone AMS grade standard.
- Capture direct PDF links and AMS pages; avoid third-party summaries; Federal Register/GPO pages acceptable when AMS PDFs aren’t available.

Deliverable format:
- For each item (1–7), provide: Item, Likely corresponding modern standard title, Supersession status (Yes/No/Uncertain), Key evidence (dates, “Supersedes”/“Revised” clauses), and URL(s). Include short notes about any renaming or consolidation that justifies mapping.
- Conclude with a compact tally: counts of Superseded Yes/No/Uncertain under interpretation A (7 items) and under interpretation B (3 items).

Comprehensive Report: Supersession Status of Selected 1959 USDA/AMS Grade Standards and Final Percentage Calculation Overview of the Task - Objective: Determine, for a defined subset of items listed in the July 2, 1959 “United States Standards for Grades of Processed Fruits, Vegetables, and Certain Other Products,” what percentage (to the nearest percent) of those standards have been superseded by a new version since that date, as of August 2023. - Inclusion rule: Consider the items in the “Dried and Dehydrated” section that are specifically marked as “Dehydrated,” plus any entries in the “Frozen/Chilled” section whose item name contains the whole name of such dehydrated items, but exclude entries that are marked “Chilled.” - Deliverables: A transparent, audit-ready result with alternative interpretations, full reasoning, sources, and explicit uncertainties. Working History and Solving Trajectory 1) Planning and setup - Created a structured plan: 1. Locate and extract the full item lists from the July 2, 1959 compilation (Dried/Dehydrated and Frozen/Chilled sections) with exact strings and pages. 2. Build the denominator set per the matching rule, documenting assumptions. 3. For each item in the denominator, determine supersession by locating authoritative USDA/AMS standards or Federal Register entries indicating revision/reissue after July 2, 1959 (and before August 2023). 4. Compute counts and percentages under all plausible interpretations, rounding to nearest percent, while documenting uncertainties. 2) Retrieval and extraction of the July 2, 1959 source - Located and used the authoritative PDF: - Title: “United States standards for grades of processed fruits, vegetables, and certain other products (as of July 2, 1959)” - URL: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/06/United_States_standards_for_grades_of_processed_fruits%2C_vegetables%2C_and_certain_other_products_%28as_of_July_2%2C_1959%29_%28IA_unitedstatesstan14unit_4%29.pdf - Internet Archive mirror: https://archive.org/details/unitedstatesstan14unit_4 - Verified key section headings and pages: - “DRIED or DEHYDRATED (Lo» -moisture)” on page 5. - “FROZEN or CHILLED (if so stated) l/” on pages 5–6 (continuation indicated). - Extracted verbatim item lines (focus on relevant subset, complete lists available in source): - Dried and Dehydrated section items (page 5): • Apples • Apples, Dehydrated (Low-moisture) 2/ • Apricots • Currants • Dates 2/ • Figs • Grapefruit Juice (Dehydrated) 2/ • Orange Juice (Dehydrated) 2/ • Peaches • Pears • Prunes • Raisins, Processed - Frozen/Chilled section items (pages 5–6; selected lines relevant to our matching rule shown): • Apples (Frozen) • Grapefruit Juice, Concentrated (Frozen) • Grapefruit Juice and Orange Juice, Concentrated, Blended (Frozen) • Orange Juice, Chilled (Chilled; excluded by rule) • Orange Juice, Concentrated (Frozen) - Notes: • OCR artifacts noted (e.g., “Feppers, Sweet” likely “Peppers, Sweet”), but unaffected items for our matching are clear. • “Grapefruit Juice and Orange Juice, Concentrated, Blended” spans two lines; presented as one entry. 3) Denominator construction and matching interpretations - The rule requires: - Include those items in the Dried/Dehydrated section specifically marked “Dehydrated.” - Add any Frozen entries that contain the whole name of the dehydrated item (string containment of the commodity name), excluding “Chilled.” - Dehydrated items (exact strings, marked “Dehydrated”): • Apples, Dehydrated (Low-moisture) 2/ • Grapefruit Juice (Dehydrated) 2/ • Orange Juice (Dehydrated) 2/ - Frozen items containing these commodity names (excluding Chilled): • Apples (contains “Apples”) • Grapefruit Juice, Concentrated (contains “Grapefruit Juice”) • Grapefruit Juice and Orange Juice, Concentrated, Blended (contains both “Grapefruit Juice” and “Orange Juice”; counted as one standard) • Orange Juice, Concentrated (contains “Orange Juice”) - Two interpretations documented: - Interpretation A (commodity-name containment): Denominator = 7 items (3 dehydrated + 4 frozen entries as above). - Interpretation B (exact-string containment of the full dehydrated line): Denominator = 3 items (only the dehydrated items themselves; no frozen entries contain the full dehydrated strings with qualifiers). 4) Supersession research and evidence gathering - Confirmed superseded item: • Apples, Dehydrated (Low-moisture) 2/ — superseded by a later issue. - Evidence: USDA/AMS official PDF stating a “second issue” with an effective date of July 31, 1977. - PDF: “United States Standards for Grades of Dehydrated (Low-Moisture) Apples” - URL: https://www.ams.usda.gov/sites/default/files/media/Dehydrated_Apples_Standard%5B1%5D.pdf - Excerpt: “Effective date July 31, 1977. This is the second issue of the United States Standards for Grades of Dehydrated (Low Moisture) Apples, published in the FEDERAL REGISTER of June 30, 1977 (42 FR 33259) to become effective July 31, 1977.” - AMS landing page: https://www.ams.usda.gov/grades-standards/dehydrated-apples-grades-and-standards - Context reference: • Federal Register Vol. 60, No. 232 (Dec 4, 1995): Interim final rule removing most voluntary U.S. grade standards from CFR; standards maintained separately thereafter. - URL: https://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/pkg/FR-1995-12-04/pdf/95-29462.pdf - Note: This removal does not itself constitute a supersession of a particular commodity standard; it explains regulatory format changes. - Items with no confirmed supersession evidence during this session (uncertain): • Grapefruit Juice (Dehydrated) 2/ • Orange Juice (Dehydrated) 2/ • Apples (Frozen) • Grapefruit Juice, Concentrated (Frozen) • Grapefruit Juice and Orange Juice, Concentrated, Blended (Frozen) • Orange Juice, Concentrated (Frozen) - Rationale for uncertainty: • No authoritative AMS/Federal Register PDFs were obtained during this session confirming post-1959 revisions for these items. • It is plausible that citrus frozen concentrates have later standards (e.g., frozen concentrated orange juice), but without direct citations found here, they remain unconfirmed. 5) Calculations and Results (nearest percent) - Interpretation A (commodity-name containment) - Denominator: 7 items - Confirmed superseded: 1 item (Dehydrated Apples; second issue effective 1977) - Percentage: 1/7 = 14.2857% → 14% (rounded to nearest percent) - Interpretation B (exact-string containment) - Denominator: 3 items - Confirmed superseded: 1 item (Dehydrated Apples; second issue effective 1977) - Percentage: 1/3 = 33.3333% → 33% (rounded to nearest percent) Uncertainties and Alternative Understandings - Matching rule ambiguity: • “Contain the whole name of the item” can reasonably be interpreted as string containment of the commodity name (e.g., “Orange Juice”) rather than the entire dehydrated line with qualifiers. We therefore present Interpretation A (commodity-name containment) as the primary case, and Interpretation B (exact-string containment) as a stricter alternative. - Supersession scope: • “Superseded by a new version” is taken to mean any official reissue/revision after July 2, 1959 (e.g., “second issue,” “revised,” “effective [later date]”). Withdrawals with no replacement would not count as superseded. - Evidence gaps: • Based on available session findings, supersession evidence was definitively confirmed only for Dehydrated Apples (1977). • Citrus frozen concentrates and dehydrated citrus juices likely have later standards, but without direct citations found here, including them as superseded would be speculative. Key Quotes and Data Extracts - 1959 Dried/Dehydrated items (subset marked “Dehydrated”): • “Apples, Dehydrated (Low-moisture) 2/” • “Grapefruit Juice (Dehydrated) 2/” • “Orange Juice (Dehydrated) 2/” - 1959 Frozen/Chilled items (relevant matches only; “Chilled” excluded): • “Apples” • “Grapefruit Juice, Concentrated” • “Grapefruit Juice and Orange Juice, Concentrated, Blended” • “Orange Juice, Concentrated” - Dehydrated Apples supersession (AMS PDF): • “Effective date July 31, 1977. This is the second issue of the United States Standards for Grades of Dehydrated (Low Moisture) Apples, published in the FEDERAL REGISTER of June 30, 1977 (42 FR 33259) to become effective July 31, 1977.” Citations - July 2, 1959 compilation: • https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/06/United_States_standards_for_grades_of_processed_fruits%2C_vegetables%2C_and_certain_other_products_%28as_of_July_2%2C_1959%29_%28IA_unitedstatesstan14unit_4%29.pdf • https://archive.org/details/unitedstatesstan14unit_4 - Dehydrated Apples standard (second issue, effective July 31, 1977): • https://www.ams.usda.gov/sites/default/files/media/Dehydrated_Apples_Standard%5B1%5D.pdf • https://www.ams.usda.gov/grades-standards/dehydrated-apples-grades-and-standards - Federal Register context (Dec 4, 1995; removal from CFR): • https://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/pkg/FR-1995-12-04/pdf/95-29462.pdf FINAL ANSWER - Primary interpretation (commodity-name containment, denominator = 7): 14% - Alternative interpretation (exact-string containment, denominator = 3): 33% Because we were able to conclusively verify supersession for only one item (Dehydrated Apples) during this session, 14% (1 of 7) is the strictly evidenced percentage to the nearest percent. Under the stricter alternative interpretation, the result is 33% (1 of 3). Further authoritative confirmations (particularly for frozen concentrated citrus standards) could raise the percentage under the primary interpretation, but such evidence was not obtained within this session.

LLM extracted final answer: **Step-by-step Analysis:** 1. Items to include: • All products in the 1959 “Dried and Dehydrated” list that are explicitly marked “Dehydrated”: – Apples, Dehydrated (Low-moisture) – Grapefruit Juice (Dehydrated) – Orange Juice (Dehydrated) • Plus any “Frozen/Chilled” items whose names contain the complete commodity names “Apples,” “Grapefruit Juice,” or “Orange Juice,” excluding those labelled “Chilled.” – Apples (Frozen) – Grapefruit Juice, Concentrated (Frozen) – Grapefruit Juice and Orange Juice, Concentrated, Blended (Frozen) – Orange Juice, Concentrated (Frozen) Denominator = 3 dehydrated items + 4 matching frozen items = 7 standards. 2. Supersession check (post-1959, pre-Aug 2023): • Dehydrated (Low-Moisture) Apples – confirmed superseded (second issue effective 31 Jul 1977). • No definitive evidence found that any of the other six standards have been re-issued; without proof they are counted as “not superseded.” Numerator (superseded) = 1. 3. Percentage superseded = 1 ÷ 7 ≈ 0.142857 → 14 % (rounded to nearest percent). **Final Answer:** \boxed{14} **Confidence:** 66 **Supporting Evidence:** The 1959 list and inclusion rules yield seven relevant standards. Only the Dehydrated Apples standard has documented replacement (1977 USDA/AMS “second issue” PDF). Thus 1 of 7, or about 14 %, have been superseded. **Potential Weaknesses:** Additional superseded versions for citrus juice concentrates may exist but were not located in the cited evidence; if they do, the true percentage would be higher. The interpretation of “contain the whole name of the item” could arguably require exact-string matches, which would change the denominator (and percentage) to 3 → 33 %.
